title: A Mission Worth Dying For
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Jesus gives us a mission, warns that some will doubt, and promises to be with us. The same Spirit who emboldened the apostles is in us.
exhortation: Jesus gives us a mission. It's amazing that he would trust us with something so important. It's basically mission impossible: save the world. And Jesus told his disciples the world would hate them. They were hated, persecuted and eventually killed for his name, as were many thousands of saints who have gone before us. We have a mission worth living for, worth fighting for and worth dying for.

I think a lot of our personal problems come from not being on mission. When we get off mission, we can become depressed, anxious and fearful. Let's get back on mission. It isn't easy, but it's where we're meant to be.

The second thing I see is that some doubted. Think about where that phrase sits in this passage. These disciples were looking at the risen Savior, and some doubted. We see people around us faced with the truth who turn away, and it can be baffling, frustrating, even devastating. But if Jesus himself dealt with this, we will too. Our job is to preach the gospel and pray for those around us. It isn't our job to save people. We leave that in the hands of Jesus.

The last point is that he will be with us. Think of Peter, who stood before the powerful people of his day, people who could destroy him, and boldly declared the gospel in the face of persecution, imprisonment and flogging. The same Spirit that was in him is in us. The takeaway isn't how awesome Peter is, but how powerful the Spirit of God is in the believer. When Jesus said, "I am with you always," he meant it. He is with us just as he was with Peter and Paul, Augustine and Martin Luther, Jonathan Edwards, Charles Spurgeon, George Whitefield, Jim Elliot and Billy Graham. What a great cloud of witnesses, examples of how God's Spirit empowers ordinary Christians.
prayer: Lord, we can only do this by the power of your grace, by the power of the cross cleansing us from our sin and making us white as snow in your sight, so that we can boldly embrace the mission you have set before us and step out onto the waters into what you've called us to.

The law of grace is now the law we live under. We are free, free indeed, by your mercy and by what you accomplished on the cross. So may we run the race and live in light of what you have done. Remind us who we are in you. In Jesus' name, amen.
